# HTML heads in the shapes of real READMEs

Each part below is one head as READMEs write it, in words of our own. The
shapes are the ones that read differently from a browser today.

<div align="center">
  <h1>Harbour</h1>
  <p>A small crate for <b>tidal</b> tables.</p>
</div>

<div align="center">

[Docs](https://example.com/docs) · [Issues](https://example.com/issues)

</div>

<div align="center">
<p>

A paragraph in a div, set apart by blank lines.

</p>
</div>

<div align="center">

A div whose end tag is on the line after another end tag.

<details>

<summary>More</summary>

Hidden text.

</details>
</div>

<details>
<summary>Closed up</summary>

Text of the details.

</details>
<p></p>

<div>

<div>

A plain div in a plain div, cut by blank lines.

</div>

</div>

<p>

A plain paragraph with blank lines round its text.

</p>

<p align="center">
  <span>A span in a centred paragraph.</span>
</p>

<br>

<sup>A superscript alone in its block.</sup>

<p align="center">

<img src="images/icon.png" alt="Icon">

</p>
